media.title: Kolonja polska w Berlinie — Kurjer Warszawski clipping, 27 March 1929
media.description: “Kolonja polska w Berlinie,” report from Kurjer Warszawski’s Berlin correspondent (signed “Zastępca”), 27 March 1929, p. 3, on Polish cultural life in Berlin over the preceding months. It records a concert of the Berlin “Harmonja,” given strictly within the Polish community and conducted by “the young composer dr. Bronisław Kaper,” with the Dresden Opera tenor Salecki and the soprano Głowacka; it also lists recitals by the pianist Róża Etkin among the colony’s concerts.

timelineEvents.title: Involvement in Polish cultural life in Berlin
timelineEvents.label: 1929 · Polish cultural life in Berlin
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper conducts a concert of the Berlin “Harmonja” given within the Polish community.
timelineEvents.longDescription: In its report on the Polish colony in Berlin, the Berlin correspondent of “Kurjer Warszawski” (27 March 1929) records that a concert of the Berlin “Harmonja,” conducted by “the young composer dr. Bronisław Kaper,” took place strictly within the Polish community, with the tenor Salecki of the Dresden Opera and the soprano Głowacka. The report covers the preceding months and gives no date for the concert; it does not describe the ensemble further.
